original_finding.title: Managed-to-independent session promotion only updates the browser envelope, not the durable session state

root_cause.summary: The adapter intentionally delays managed-session takeover until a post-outage request proves the same cross-Agent ownership boundary as a fresh disaster login, but once that proof succeeds it mutates only `request.session.stcontrol`. The serialized durable session record, its `activityEpoch` / `controllerGeneration`, the active-independent counters, and the first pending-sync marker all continue to read from the stale managed record.
evidence: src/stcontrol.js:518-523 explicitly says confirmed outage must clear managed leases immediately but must not convert sessions until a later request proves ownership.
src/stcontrol.js:623-636 and src/stcontrol.js:676-724 define the ownership/quorum gate used by disaster login and request-path promotion.
src/stcontrol.js:945-953 updates only the browser envelope to `independent`, resets `activityEpoch` to 0, and copies the current controller generation after `canUseNativeLogin()` succeeds.

src/stcontrol.js:982-999 reuses `current.sessions[sessionId]` without overwriting `loginMode`, `activityEpoch`, or `controllerGeneration`, so the durable record stays `managed` and the `independent_write` marker at lines 997-998 never fires for a promoted session.
src/stcontrol.js:482-489, src/stcontrol.js:553-555, and src/stcontrol.js:1030-1037 count active independent sessions and report telemetry from the durable record, not the browser envelope.
src/stcontrol.js:526-531 seeds draining-time pending-sync facts only from durable independent sessions, so a promoted-but-not-durable session is invisible to the recovery boundary.
tests/stcontrol-adapter.node.test.mjs:762-799 currently locks in the stale behavior by asserting that the durable session remains `managed` after outage transition.

internal/agent/control_mode.go:233-241 and internal/store/control_modes.go:230-249 refuse `independent-draining -> managed` only when adapter-reported `ActiveIndependentSessions` or `PendingUserSyncs` stay non-zero, so under-reporting directly weakens the managed-recovery fence.

identity_boundary: Round 28 discussion.md:899-909 requires existing logged-in users not to be dropped unconditionally when controller failure is confirmed.
Round 29 discussion.md:928-944 restricts disaster write access to the last active node.
Round 30 discussion.md:965-970 allows takeover on another node only after system judgement plus user confirmation.
users-public.js:171-195 applies the explicit password + takeover path for fresh independent login.

remediation_plan.strategy: Preserve the Round28 session-continuity rule and the existing ownership proof boundary, but durably promote the session inside the same serialized request-admission mutation that follows a successful independent-ownership decision.

steps.change: Keep `applyStcontrolMode()` fail-closed behavior as-is: clear managed leases on confirmed outage, but do not bulk-convert all sessions there.

In `stcontrolRequestTracker()`, carry an explicit `promotedToIndependent` flag after `canUseNativeLogin()` succeeds, then inside the existing `mutateState()` admission block overwrite the durable session's `loginMode`, `activityEpoch=0`, and `controllerGeneration` to match the newly authorized independent envelope.
Evaluate `pendingSyncUsers` after that durable overwrite so the first post-promotion write persists an `independent_write` marker immediately.

Update the outage regression to drive `stcontrolRequestTracker()` through a successful ownership proof and assert that the durable session is now `independent`, `activityEpoch` is zeroed, `controllerGeneration` is refreshed, telemetry reports `independent`, and a write creates a durable pending-sync marker.

Add a recovery-boundary regression proving that after promotion plus an independent write, `applyStcontrolMode(DRAINING)` reports non-zero `active_independent_sessions` / `pending_user_syncs`, `markUserSynchronized()` rejects while the session is still active, and only logout or idle expiry plus exact marker completion allows the node back to managed.

remediation_plan.rollback: If the product intentionally changes to 'existing managed cookies must always re-login during disaster mode', remove request-path promotion entirely. Otherwise the safe rollback for this fix is to revert only the targeted durable-session overwrite and its regressions; no schema change is involved.

benefits: Preserves the Round28 requirement that already logged-in users are not unconditionally dropped during confirmed controller outage.
Keeps the existing ownership/quorum proof boundary instead of silently auto-promoting all sessions at mode-switch time.
Makes `activeIndependentSessions`, telemetry, `pendingUserSyncs`, and draining reconciliation observe the same independent identity the browser is already using.
Restores the `independent-draining -> managed` fence that Agent and Store already implement.
risks: A careless implementation could mark a session independent before ownership proof actually succeeded.
Using stale pre-mutation controller-generation data could preserve the wrong disaster-generation stamp on the durable session.
mitigations: Gate the durable overwrite behind a local boolean set only after `canUseNativeLogin()` returns `{ allowed: true }` or after a fresh independent login path has already registered an independent session.
Write the durable session fields inside the serialized `mutateState()` block and source the generation from the current state used for persistence.
Add regressions for both the successful promotion path and the denied-promotion path.

reassessed_severity.justification: The bug is not just telemetry drift. It suppresses the exact adapter facts that Agent and Store use to hold the node in `independent-draining`, so a recovered controller can be told the node is fully drained while a browser is still writing under an independent cookie. The later managed-mode fence can then be reopened on false zero/zero evidence.
